$comment: One description per field of schema/report-v1.schema.json, keyed by path. The generator fails if a field has no description or a description has no field. Wording follows the comments in src/types.ts, src/scan.ts, src/report.ts, src/epss.ts and the README.
schemaVersion: Report format version. Minor and patch versions only add optional fields; a breaking change bumps the major version.
tool: The tool that produced the report.
tool.name: Always relvet.
tool.version: Relvet version that produced the report.
generatedAt: When the report was created, in UTC.
durationMs: How long the vulnerability lookups took, in milliseconds.
mock: True only for runs on the bundled mock data (RELVET_MOCK=1), which is never a real scan.
input.file: Name of the lockfile or SBOM, as given or relative to the working directory.
input.dependencies: Packages checked, deduplicated by ecosystem, name and version.
input.skipped: Entries that could not be checked: local, git or workspace links, and SBOM components without a supported purl.
cra: The CRA applicability screen. Not legal advice.
cra.rule: ID of the rule that produced the verdict.
cra.reason: Why the rule applies, in plain English.
cra.answers: The three answers the verdict is based on.
cra.answers[].question: Question text.
cra.answers[].answer: The answer; unknown when it was not given.
cra.keyDates: CRA dates and what applies from each.
cra.keyDates[].inForce: Whether the date had passed when the report was generated.
summary: Counts over all issues, not only the ten the text output prints.
summary.vulnerablePackages: Packages with at least one issue.
summary.criticalOrHigh: Issues with critical or high severity.
summary.activelyExploited: Issues with a CVE in the CISA KEV catalog.
summary.uncheckedDependencies: Packages OSV could not be asked about, for example during an outage. Anything above 0 means the result is incomplete.
sources[].name: The data source.
sources[].status: partial or unavailable means some data is missing.
sources[].message: What went wrong, or a note such as a cached KEV catalog being used.
issues: One entry per issue and package. Sorted: actively exploited (KEV) first, then EPSS, then CVSS.
issues[].package.ecosystem: OSV ecosystem, for example npm, PyPI or Maven. Empty for packages queried by purl.
issues[].package.name: Package name.
issues[].package.purl: Set for deb and apk SBOM components, which are queried by purl.
issues[].aliases: Other IDs of the same issue, including advisories merged into this one.
issues[].cves: CVE IDs among the ID and aliases.
issues[].severity.level: Severity level, from the CVSS v3.x score or the advisory's own label.
issues[].severity.score: CVSS v3.x base score computed from the advisory's vector; null without a v3 vector.
issues[].severity.vector: The advisory's CVSS vector, if it has one.
issues[].fixedVersions: Fixed versions in the advisory's affected ranges for this package.
issues[].recommendedFix: The version to upgrade to: the fix for the range that contains the installed version, else the nearest higher fix. Null when none is published.
issues[].kev: The CISA KEV catalog entry when a CVE of this issue is listed; otherwise null.
issues[].kev.dateAdded: Date CISA added it to the catalog.
issues[].kev.dueDate: Due date from the catalog entry.
issues[].kev.knownRansomwareCampaignUse: True when the catalog marks the CVE as known to be used in ransomware campaigns.
issues[].kev.name: Vulnerability name from the catalog.
issues[].epss: The highest EPSS score among the issue's CVEs; null when none was scored.
issues[].epss.score: Probability of exploitation activity in the next 30 days.
issues[].references: Up to 10 reference URLs from the advisory.
issues[].detailsAvailable: False when OSV returned the ID but its details could not be fetched.
